Woman searches for 10 puppies stolen from White County backyard

A White County woman is searching for 10 stolen five-week-old puppies after spotting what she believes is a Craigslist ad selling them, and says police are working to track down the seller before the unvaccinated puppies' health is put at risk.

Actual Article Body:
What This Story Is About

Why It Matters

What Happens Next

Catch Up

WHITE COUNTY, Tenn. (WSMV) - A woman is searching for 10 puppies she says were stolen from her backyard, with a Craigslist post allegedly selling the puppies as her only lead.

Sandra Moore said her backyard, usually filled with the sound of small puppies playing and eating, has been quiet since Tuesday morning, when someone stole the puppies as the sun came up.

Moore said she let the 10 five-week-old Borzoi puppies out around 5:30 a.m. to run around and spend time with their mother.

“I was in the house for about an hour and I came back out with the food and the dogs were gone,” Moore said.

Moore said she initially thought the puppies may have escaped on their own but quickly realized the pen they were in could not have been undone by the puppies. She said the gate has to be undone and woven through to be opened.

Moore said the puppies’ mother, Emira, took off after the thief and came back with a gash across her face.

Moore called police, and on Wednesday she came across a Craigslist ad selling her puppies.

“When I saw that, that just about put me over the edge,” Moore said.

Moore said police are working to subpoena information from the account allegedly selling her puppies, but said that could take days.

Moore said she typically keeps the puppies for three to six months before placing them in their forever home. She said the puppies, at five weeks old, have not weaned from their mother or received any vaccinations.

Moore said their lives are in danger if they are not receiving proper care.

“I would be happy to buy these dogs back. I don’t want anyone out money, I am happy to be out the money. I just don’t want my dogs to die,” Moore said.

Moore said anyone who recognizes the puppies or has information should contact the White County Sheriff’s Office.

By KYLIE STEVENS, SENIOR BREAKING NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  09:48 AEDT, 23 October 2026   |  Updated:  10:43 AEDT, 23 October 2026

A police investigation has been launched after the bodies of a woman and child were found outside a 30-storey high-rise apartment tower.

Emergency services were called to Prospect Street in Box Hill, in Melbourne's eastern suburbs, about 6.20pm Thursday after reports that a woman had been found unresponsive.

Police rushed to the scene where they located the woman's body on the footpath and an unresponsive primary school-aged child nearby.

The pair could not be revived and died at the scene.

The vicinity was cordoned off for much of the night as detectives investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

'At this early stage, police are not looking for anyone else in relation to the incident,' Victoria Police said in a statement.

It's unclear whether the pair lived at the 199-apartment Promenade complex.

Shocked residents knew very little about what had happened.

The  grim discovery was made in Box Hill shortly before 6.30pm on Thursday night

Many residents received texts from police asking them to remain inside on Thursday night, whole others were blocked from entering or existing the complex.

'I just feel a little terrified that it happened in my building,' one woman told The Age.

Anyone who witnessed the incident or has information is urged to contact Crime Stoppers.

The post 99-yo Woman Snags ‘World’s Oldest Wing-Walker’ Title – 3 Months After Another Gran Did It (LOOK) appeared first on Good News Network.

Actual Article Body:
A 99-year-old has become the world’s oldest wing-walker—just three months after her niece saw another elderly woman do it, and the staff at her assisted-living facility urged her to try.

This week, Guinness World Records officially bestowed the title on Helga Duffy, who was strapped to the top of a small plane at Rendcomb Airfield in Gloucestershire, England.

She broke their world record for wing-walking just three months after the title was nabbed by a 97-year-old woman named Betty Bromage.

“I had no idea what it was,” Helga said, of the aviation stunt.

At 99, she had been saying that it was “the last time” she could “do something different”—and when she saw what wing-walking entailed, she was determined to try it.

Despite initial concerns about getting on the plane itself, due to her arthritis and a bad right knee, Helga spent over five minutes in the air—wearing special clothing. (Watch the video below…)

“It was a very different sensation than I’ve ever had,” said the woman who spent most of her life working as a nurse.

“Once we did the round and we were up a thousand meters, I took three deep breaths; the air up there is so pure you wouldn’t believe it.

“I thought to myself, ‘come on now!’”

“I felt so good, I thought, ‘is this like if you take drugs?’ I’m sure it is.

Strapped in tightly, she felt “very safe”, and upon landing Helga met an official adjudicator from Guinness World Records.

Will Munford presented her with an official certificate when she touched down after the flight.

“It was a wonderful atmosphere,” said Helga’s niece, Jackie Rose, who saw news reports this year of Betty Bromage winning the title, and realized it was possible for Helga.

“Everybody was clapping. I had so much admiration for her because I knew how painful it was on her knee.”

“It was so nice just to see, age is irrelevant. It’s just lovely to see somebody doing something they enjoy.”

The certificate is being displayed in the senior care facility as a reminder that age is just a number.

“Try anything,” said Helga, who also raised over £1,600 ($2,000) for the regional Air Ambulance charity with her stunt.

“Don’t ever say, ‘I can’t do it’. You can’t ‘see’ until you’ve tried… It’s my motto.”

When asked about the new record-holder, Betty congratulated Helga on her success, “joking that she was excited to turn 100 and beat the new record”.

Jackie told the BBC that she’s wanted to prove that “even though she’s 99, she’s still that lady she was years and years ago.”
